senses: heart, conscience (seat of the thoughts and will)
la:noun:mens.html:
mens, mentis (
nom. sing. mentis: terra corpus est, at mentis ignis est, Enn. ap. P.; so too, istic est de sole sumptus; isque totus mentis est, Enn. ap. Müll.; cf. and 7 Vahl.), f.
from the root men, whence memini, q. v., and comminiscor
, the mind, disposition; the heart, soul (class.).
In gen.: fusi sine mente ac sine sensu ullo jaceant, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 134 Vahl.): nubilam mentem Animi habeo,: mens animi,: mens animi vigilat,: mala mens, malus animus,bad disposition, bad heart,: hominum erga se mentes,feelings, sentiments,: mens mollis ad calamitates perferendas,: humanae mentis vitium ... saeva cupido,.—
In partic.
The conscience: cum vero jurato sententia dicenda est, meminerit, deum se adhibere testem, id est ut ego arbitror, mentem suam,: auditor, cui frigida mens est crimi nibus,: quos diri conscia fact, Mens habet attonitos et surdo verbere caedit,.—
The intellectual faculties, the mind, understanding, intellect, reason, judgment, discernment, consideration, reflection, etc.: mens, cui regnum totius animi (soul) a naturā tributum est, : animus ita est constitutus, ut habeat praestantiam mentis,: deorum mente atque ratione omnem mundum administrari et regi,: mente complecti aliquid,to comprehend, understand,: sanum mentis esse,to be of sound mind,: mens sana in corpore sano, Juv 10, 356: mentis suae esse,to be in one's right mind, in one's senses,; so, mentis compotem esse,: captus mente, out of his senses, beside himself, mad (cf. menceps), ; , a, 11: mentem amittere,to lose one's mind,. 31: mentis inops,: huic ex tempore dicenti effluit mens,his recollection vanished,: quis est tam vecors, qui ea, quae tanta mente fiunt, casu putet posse fieri?: vobis dent mentem oportet (di), ut prohibeatis, sicut mihi dederunt, ut, etc.,: quid tibi istuc in mentem venit?what comes into your mind? what are you thinking of?: modo hercle in mentem venit,: venit hoc mihi in mentem, te, etc.,: venit in mentem, ut, etc.,.—With inf., .—With nom.: miserae ubi venit in mentem mortis metus,: servi venere in mentem calliditates,: quotiescumque patria in mentem veniret,; ; ; cf.: numquam ea res tibi tam belle in mentem venire potuisset,; .—With gen. (so mostly in Cic.): non minus saepe ei venit in mentem potestatis, quam aequitatis tuae,he bethought himself of,: tibi tuarum virtutum veniat in mentem,: venit mihi Platonis in mentem,: solet mihi in mentem venire illius temporis,.—
Mind, thought, plan, purpose, intention, design. quā facere id possis, nostram nunc accipe mentem, : ut nemini dubium esse debeat, quin reliquo tempore eādem mente sim futurus,

: Dolabella classem eā mente comparavit, ut,: mentes deorum scrutari in fibris,: ferro percussit, sed non occidendi mente, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 1, 6, 3: poenae modus ex mente facientis statui potest,: in mente est mihi dormire,I have a mind to,.—

Spirit, boldness, courage: addere mentem, to give courage to, Hor Ep. 2, 2, 36: demittunt mentes,lose courage, (cf. animus).—
Personified: Mens, the goddess of thought, whose festival was held on the eighth of June, : Menti aedem T. Octacilius praetor vovit,; cf. .

la:verb:mentior.html:
mentĭor, ītus, 4 (
fut. mentibitur, for mentietur, ; ; v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 448), v. dep. n. and a. [prob. from root men-, whence mens, memini, q. v. Original meaning, to invent; hence],
Neutr., to lie, cheat, deceive, etc.: mentiri palam,: mentire,: adversus aliquem,: apud aliquem,: sibi,: mihi,; : aperte,: in re aliquā,: de re aliquā,: adeo veritatis diligens, ut ne joco quidem mentiretur,.—With acc. and inf., to pretend, to declare falsely: certam me sum mentitus habere Horam, quae, etc.,; : mentior nisi or si mentior, a form of asseveration, I am a liar, if, etc.: mentior, nisi et quae alunt illud, corpora sunt,: si mentiar, inquit, Ultima, quā fallam, sit Venus illa mihi,.—Of things, to deceive, impose upon: frons, oculi, vultus persaepe mentiuntur, oratio vero saepissime, : in quibus nihil umquam ... vetustas mentita sit,.—
To deceive one's self, mistake: mentire, gnate, Brix ad loc.—
Act., to lie or speak falsely about, to assert falsely, make a false promise about; to feign, counterfeit, imitate a shape, nature, etc.: cujus consilio tantam rem mentitus esset,had devised such a falsehood,: originem alicujus,: auspicium,: titulum Lyciscae,to assume falsely,: noctem,to promise falsely,: cur sese daemonia mentiuntur,; also, to invent, feign, of a poetical fiction: ita mentitur (sc. Homerus),; cf.: poëtae Orionem mentiuntur in pelago incidentem,.—Pass.: si a debitore, praelato die, pignoris obligatio mentiatur,.—
Trop., of inanim. subjects: semel fac illud, Mentitur tua quod subinde tussis, do what your cough keeps falsely promising, i. e. die, : mentiris juvenem tinctis capillis,: color, qui chrysocollam mentitur,: nec varios discet mentiri lana colores,: sexum viris denegatum muliebri motu, Col. praef. 1.—Hence, *
mentĭens, entis, m.subst., a fallacy, sophism: quomodo mentientem, quem ψευδόμενον vocant, dissolvas, . —
mentītus, a, um, Part., in pass. signif., imitated, counterfeit, feigned (poet.): mentita tela,: figurae,: fama,: nomen,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; Poët. ap. ; . mentiti fictique terrores,; : divinitas,; .

la:noun:mensis.html:
mensis, is (
gen. plur. regularly mensium; freq. mensum,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; v. Neue, Formenl. 1. p. 265 sq.), m.
root ma-, measure; Sanscr mas; Gr. μην, the measure of time; cf. Goth. mena; Germ. Mond; Engl. moon, month
, a month.
Lit.: mensium nomina, Müll.; Censor 22: hunc mensem vortentem servare, the return of this month, i. e. a full year, : septem menses sunt. quom in hasce aedis pedem nemo mtro tulit, id Most. 2, 2, 39: lunae cursus qui, quia mensa spatia conficiunt, menses nominantur,: annūm novūm voluerunt esse primum mensem Martium, Atta ap : primo mense,at the beginning of the month,: regnavit is quidem paucos menses,; Hor C. 2, 9, 6.—
Esp., plur., the months, i. e. the fixed time, the period: mensis jam tibi actos vides,.—
Transf., esp. in plur., the menses: prodest mulierum mensibus retardatis,; ; ; 23, 7, 71, § 138 et saep.—In sing.: a muliere incitati mensis,; .—Transf., of female animals, the yearly flux,

la:noun:mentio.html:
mentĭo, ōnis, f.
from root man-, men-; v. memini
,
a calling to mind, a cursory speaking of, a making mention, mentioning, naming, mention: civitatis,: casu in eorum mentionem incidi,accidentally happened to mention them,: tui,mention of you,: Graecorum,.—With a foll. ut: mentionem fecit, ut reperirem, etc.,: mentione illatā a tribunis, ut liceret,; : mentionem facere alicujus rei,to make mention of a thing, mention it,: mentionem de aliquā re,: de quo feci supra mentionem,: mentionem movere alicujus rei,: mentionem habere accusatorum,to make mention of, to mention,: mentionem rei incohare,: mentionem condicionum jacere,: mentionem facere, with acc. and inf., to mention: noli facere mentionem, te has emisse,: in senatu consules faciunt mentionem, placere statui, si, etc.,: mentio in senatu facta,; : qua de re tecum mentionem feceram,: fac mentionem cum avonculo,: ubi mentionem ego fecero de puellā, mihi ut despondeat,to propose for a girl,.—In plur.: secessionis mentiones ad vulgus militum sermonibus occultis serere,suggestions, hints,.

senses: a table of food; meal, course, feast
la:noun:mensa.html:
mensa, ae,
f [Sanscr, ma, measure; Gr. μέτρον; cf. manus, mane, etc.], a table for any purpose, as a dining-table; a market-stand for meat, vegetables, etc.; a money-dealer's table or counter, a sacrificial table, etc.
Lit. Of the table itself as a fabrid: non ferre mensam nisi crebris distinctam venis,: mensa inanis nunc si adponatur mihi,: cibos in mensam alicui apponere,: surgunt a mensā saturi, poti,: ad mensam consistere. to wait at table, : auferre mensam,: apud mensam,at table,; ; : arae vicem praestare posse mensam dicatam,.—
Transf.
Food; a table, meal, course: quocum mensam sermonesque suos impertit, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 240 Vahl.): communicabo te semper mensā meā,: ita mensas exstruit,: parciore mensā uti,: Italicae Syracusiaeque mensae,: cui Quintus de mensa misit,; so, parāsti mensam adversus eos qui tribulant me,: una mensa,at a single meal,: prior, proxima mensa, the first, the second rank at table; the first or second in esteem: Raeticis uvis prior mensa erat,; : secunda mensa, the second course, the dessert (at which much wine was used), Cels 1, 2: haec ad te scripsi, appositā secundā mensā,during the dessert,; : Agesilaus coronas secundamque mensam servis dispertiit, Nep Ages. 8, 4: secunda mensa bono stomacho nihil nocet,, fin.: mensae tempore,meal-time,.—
The guests at table: cum primum istorum conduxit mensa choragum,.—
A money-changer's counter: decem minas dum hic solvit, omnis mensas transiit,: mensam poni jubet atque Effundi saccos nummorum,: nummulariorum,: publica,a public bank,; .—
A butcher's table: mensa lanionia,butcher's stall, shambles,.—
Mensa lusoria, a gaming-table (late Lat.), .—
A sacrificial table: Curiales mensae, in quibus immolabatur Junoni, quae Curis est appellata, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. Curiales, p. 64 Müll.: mensae deorum,: Jovis mensa,: a small altar: super tumulum statuere,.—
The long flat part, the table, of a military engine (e. g. of a catapult), .—
A stand or platform on which slaves were exposed for sale: servus de mensā paratus,; .

mendax, dācis, adj.
mentior
,

Lit.: mendacem esse adversus aliquem,: cum mendaci homini, ne verum quidem dicenti, credere soleamus,: Carthaginienses fraudulenti et mendaces,: aretalogus,.—As subst.: mendax, dācis, m., a liar.—Prov.: mendacem memorem esse oportet,a liar should have a good memory,.— Comp.: Parthis mendacior,.—Sup.: mendacissimus,the greatest liar,.—With gen.: si hujus rei me mendacem esse inveneris,.—With dat.: saepe fui mendax pro te mihi,.—With in and acc.: in parentem,; for which adversum, .— With in and abl.: in tenui farragine,.—
Transf., of inanim, and abstr. things, lying, false, deceptive; feigned, fictitious, counterfeit, not real, etc. (mostly poet.): mendacia visa,: speculum,: fundus,that does not yield the expected fruits,: damnum,: infamia,: os,: pennae,: quidquid Graecia mendax audet in historia,.—Hence, adv.: mendācĭter, falsely, mendaciously (post-class.): praedicare,.— Sup.: mendacissime dicere,.

Lit.: mensuram facere alicujus, Ov A. A. 3, 265: agere,to measure, survey,: inire. Col 5, 3: res (quae) pondere numero mensura constant,.—
Transf., a measure, by which any thing is measured: majore mensurā reddere,: qui modus mensurae medimnus appellatur,kind of measure,: mensuras et pondera invenit Phidon Argivus, aut Palamedes,: ex aquā, i. e. clepsydra,: quicquid sub aurium mensuram aliquam cadit, numerus vocatur,: de mensura jus dicere,. —
Trop., measure, quantity, proportion, capacity, power, extent, degree, etc.: dare alicui mensuram bibendi,to prescribe how much one may drink,: nostri orbis,: beneficii,: qui tanti mensuram nominis imples,i. e. who answerest to its meaning, art worthy of it,: ficti crescit,measure, size,: sui, one's own measure, i. e. capacity, : sed deerat pisci patinae mensura,was too small,: nuribus Argolicis fui Mensura voti, I was the measure of their wishes, i. e. they desired to have as much as I possessed, : submittere se ad mensuram discentis,to accommodate one's self to the capacity of the learner,: legati, character, standing. : mensura tamen quae sufficiat census,how large a fortune,—In painting: Apelles cedebat Asclepiodoro de mensuris, hoc est quanto quid a quoque distare deberet,the degree of prominence, and relative distances, of parts of a picture,.—In gram.: mensurae verborum,the quantities of their syllables,.
